title: A Caesar shift with char arithmetic

blocks.text: `char` is one of the eight primitive types: an unsigned 16-bit number that happens to print as a character. `'a' + 1` is the `int` `98`, and `(char) ('a' + 1)` is `'b'`.

Write `CaesarShift.shift(String text, int k)`, where `0 <= k <= 25`. Every ASCII letter moves `k` places on in the alphabet, wrapping from `z` back to `a`, and keeps its case. Every other character is unchanged.

cases.says: It moves lowercase letters k places on.
A letter moved past z wraps round to the start of the alphabet.
Digits, spaces and punctuation are not moved.

concepts: char is an unsigned 16-bit number: char arithmetic is int arithmetic and needs a cast back.
